app.meta_description: Lightcutoff is a project that aims to collect data on the supply of electrical energy in Cameroon, these data are mainly provided by people directly concerned by these cuts (the population).

about.title: About us
about.content: In Cameroon, access to public resources such as electricity and water is not easy. Some regions may even be deprived of it for several days or even weeks. The {projectTitle} project aims to help make a real time inventory of access to electricity in Cameroon. This, in order to allow third parties to adapt their daily life and to be informed

aboutus.title: Who are we?
aboutus.text_obj_1: The platform {projectTitle} aims to help make an inventory of the state of play on the power cuts in the country. This by relying on consumers. In order to help them adapt to the various interruptions
aboutus.text_obj_2: Our strategy is to provide an interactive map from where our users can report light cuts when they start and also when they end and thus inform the community.

tuto.title_page: Tutorial, learning how to use our tool
tuto.report_alert_2: In this tutorial we consider that a report is also a report, an alert and vice versa.
tuto.report_alert_1: For the moment, {projectTitle} is only available in Cameroon. This means that no report will be accepted if it is made outside Cameroon.
tuto.text_presentation: {projectTitle} is designed to help power users adapt to the constraints of power outages. This is done by means of an interactive map that would allow them to report any power outage or power restoration at their location.
tuto.legend_intro: To begin with, here is the legend of our map.
tuto.legend_text_1: As you can see, there's a specific record for each situation. We have:
tuto.legend_text_2: Marqueur bleu: To report your position on the map.
tuto.legend_text_3: Marqueur rouge: Represents a light cut reported by another user.
tuto.legend_text_4: Marqueur orange:Represents a light cut reported by yourself.
tuto.legend_text_5: Marqueur vert:Represents the end of a cut reported by you or another user.
tuto.cluster_text_1: a cluster is an area with a large number of markers. Depending on the number of markers, we have several types of clusters.
tuto.cluster_text_2: Clusters are classified according to the number of markers in the area. Thus, the order of colors ranges from blue for a relatively small number to purple for a very large number of markers.
tuto.begin_text_1: When you arrive on our map, you will be geolocated and your position will be represented by a blue marker.
tuto.begin_text_2: It is possible that your position is not exactly accurate, so to improve it we have provided a search module that will allow you to better locate yourself in the map.
tuto.begin_text_3: If it turns out that you have to move your blue marker over a very long distance, you don't necessarily have to drag it all the way. A double click on a place on the map will suffice.
tuto.begin_text_4: To add a report, simply click once on your blue marker and a form will appear. All you have to do is choose a date and time corresponding to a power outage.
tuto.report_signal_text_1: After creating a report, there are 2 possibilities:
tuto.report_signal_text_2: You report a current outage: after saving the previous report, you are presented with a new form, but you are not obliged to fill it in. You will notice an orange marker that indicates a power outage in progress that you have reported and that only you can report finished.
tuto.report_signal_text_3: To close an issued outage report, simply click on the corresponding orange marker and fill in the form.
tuto.report_signal_text_4: Another form is offered to you to complete your report: Just after you have created a report, a new form is presented to you. By filling out and sending this form, you close the power outage report initiated earlier.
tuto.after_signal_text_1: After closing an issued report (section: Reporting a power failure), you will see a green marker. To let users know that your previous outage report is no longer valid. The situation has returned to normal (power restored).

faq.title: FAQ
faq.response_1: {projectTitle} is currently only available in Cameroon. Our immediate goal is to target the Cameroonian market. Of course, we do not rule out one day being able to export it to other regions of Africa
faq.question_2: How to report a light cut on {projectTitle}?
faq.response_2:
There are two ways to report a light cut with {projectTitle}. You can find how to do this in at least 2 tutorials on our platform:
  1. In the homepage you will find a button for a video tutorial.
  2. In the footer you will also find a link to a tutorial.
